## Face form of the gravity work (`gravity-work: face`, `face-wallc`) {#sec-ch06-face}

### Summary

The face form books, in cell $i$, the work the scheme's own $x_1$ mass fluxes do against gravity: each face's
flux carries mass from the face potential to the cell's centroid potential. Its derivation is the template of
@eq-ch06-dwork-booked with $P=\mathrm{PE}_d$, written out as @eq-ch06-dwork-face in @sec-ch06-dwork. This section
covers what the code does around it: it replaces the cell work the forcing added, it adds the curvature flux for
the high-order reconstructions, it keeps the cell work in the wall cells under `face-wallc`, and it needs the
implicit operator to carry it when an implicit scheme is on.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Books the $x_1$ gravity work as a potential-energy flux difference across a cell, @eq-ch06-dwork-face.

**Data.** Reads the total $x_1$ mass flux $F$ on the two faces, face and centroid potentials; writes the energy row.

**Placement.** Each stage, after the $x_1$ flux is final and after the forcings; replaces the cell work.

**Activation.** `gravity-work: face` (the default) or `face-wallc`; turns the fixer off. $\mathcal K$ needs a
uniform $x_1$: a deck that declares a stretched one is refused.

**Guarantee / limits.** Plain `face`: $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ exact to round-off; second order, fourth interior with $\mathcal K$.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch06-face-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $m_{1,i}=\rho_iv_{1,i}$ the $x_1$ momentum density of cell $i$
[kg m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$] (appendix A $m_1$[^rg-fafd93c288d7]; code `rhov`); $\mathcal K$ the curvature flux of appendix A, notation group 3; $b_i$ the
per-cell term of the conservation sum [J], $N_{\mathrm{rd}}$ the number of roundings in one $b_i$ and $\eta_i$ its
relative rounding error.

With `gravity-work: face` the corrected-PE work of @sec-ch06-dwork is on by default
(`SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT`); this section describes the face form with that switch off, which is how the
plain face-form tests run. The curvature flux is "$\mathcal K$" in the derivation note.[^ch06-face-src]

[^ch06-face-src]: The face form and the fixer came in with chengcli/snapy#283.

### Derivation

The stage adds the cell work $W^{\mathrm{cell}}$ through the forcing (@sec-ch06-cell). The face form replaces it:
the energy row receives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta E_i &\leftarrow \Delta E_i + \Delta t\,\big(W^{\mathrm{face}}_i - W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i - \nabla_{\!1}\!\cdot g_1\mathcal K\big),\\
\mathcal K_{i-1/2} &= \tfrac{1}{12}(x_{1,i}-x_{1,i-1})(m_{1,i}-m_{1,i-1}),
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-face-energy}

with $\mathcal K=0$ on every physical $x_1$ face, and $\mathcal K$ present only for cp3, cp5 and weno5 reconstructions in
$x_1$, only with the corrected-PE work of @sec-ch06-dwork off, and only on a uniform $x_1$ grid. The last
condition is a refusal, not a degradation. @eq-ch06-face-energy writes $\mathcal K$ as a two-point difference
whose divergence is the $\tfrac{h^2}{12}\partial_1^2$ correction when the two cells have the same width; the
code states that no two-point form is exact on unequal cells and refuses the combination there rather than
running a wrong $\mathcal K$ ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). A deck that declares
a stretched $x_1$ is told to use the corrected-PE work instead (the Code layer below). The report has not
re-derived that non-existence.
@eq-ch06-face-energy is booked as `gravity_energy_correction`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}),
with the curvature term from `curv_flux1`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

The face form conserves $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ exactly on a closed column. The argument has four steps.

1. The code forms $W^{\mathrm{face}}_i=\big(\phi_i\Delta_i[AF]-\Delta_i[A\phi F]\big)/V_i$ from one face product $A\phi F$ per
   face, stored once and read by both neighbours (`potential_flux1`, `potential_flux_div`).
2. The density changes by $V_i\dot\rho_i=-\Delta_i[AF]$, so $V_i(W^{\mathrm{face}}_i+\phi_i\dot\rho_i)=-\Delta_i[A\phi F]$.
3. Summed over the column, $-\sum_i\Delta_i[A\phi F]$ telescopes to the two walls, where $F=0$: zero.
4. $\mathcal K$ is a face flux, set to zero on both physical faces, so $\sum_iV_i\nabla_{\!1}\!\cdot g_1\mathcal K=0$ by
   the same telescoping.

Round-off is the one place this shows. Write the computed per-cell terms as $\hat b_i=b_i(1+\eta_i)$, with
$\sum_ib_i=0$ exactly and $\lvert\eta_i\rvert\le N_{\mathrm{rd}}\,\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ for the $N_{\mathrm{rd}}$ roundings of one
cell term. Summing $n_1$[^rg-bf06c25d4aa7] such terms adds one rounding per addition, and to first order the error of a sum is the sum
over its additions of the partial sum times that addition's rounding (as in @sec-ch09-framework). The stage
combination $w_0^{(s)}\mathbf U^n+w_1^{(s)}\mathbf U+w_2^{(s)}\Delta\mathbf U$ then rounds each $E_i$ five times, three products and
two additions (`wght0`, [`pyharp integrator.cpp:120`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L120)), as the deposit of @sec-ch06-fixer rounds its addition to $E_i$. Together,

$$
\Big\lvert\sum_i\hat b_i\Big\rvert \le (N_{\mathrm{rd}}+n_1)\,\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_i\lvert b_i\rvert
+ 5\cdot\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_iV_i\lvert E_i\rvert \quad\text{per stage}.
$$

Counting the floating-point operations of the face-work lines and the product with $V$ gives $N_{\mathrm{rd}}\le12$, an
upper count, not a measurement. For $n_1=256$ the first term is $3.0\times10^{-14}$ of $\sum_i\lvert b_i\rvert$.
`cellface_check.py` `[C1]` measures the work identity alone, $\lvert\sum_iV_i(W^{\mathrm{face}}_i+\phi_i\dot\rho_i)\rvert$ over
$\sum_iV_i\lvert W^{\mathrm{face}}_i\rvert$, at $3.9\times10^{-15}$ on Cartesian and spherical-polar columns, inside the first
term; the energy-update term is not part of that check. `[C4]` measures the $\mathcal K$ divergence sum at
$1.3\times10^{-17}$. Its purpose
is accuracy. A
high-order reconstruction's face flux exceeds the point value $m_1$ by $\tfrac{h^2}{12}(\partial_1^2m_1+\dots)$, and the
face form books that excess as work; $\nabla_{\!1}\!\cdot g_1\mathcal K$ removes the $\partial_1^2m_1$ part. Against
the exact cell average of $g_1m_1$ and with exact point fluxes, the face form is second order in interior and wall
cells, and the face form with $\mathcal K$ is fourth order in the interior and first order in the two wall cells,
where $\mathcal K$ is present on one face only (`[C3]`, `[C4]`; orders 2.00 and 2.00, then 3.99 and 1.00, at
$n_1$ = 128 to 256). `face-wallc` books $W^{\mathrm{cell}}$ in the two wall cells, so its defect is
exactly their cell-minus-face work (`[C5]`). `[C26]` and `[C27]` of `derivation_check.py` check the first-order sum
error and the telescoping.[^ch06-face-chk]

[^ch06-face-chk]: [sha: snapy@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5; deck: the check itself; run:
    `python3 src/snapy_report/ch06/checks/cellface_check.py`, CPU, double, 1 process;

### Numerical method

@fig-ch06-face-stencil shows what the face form reads: the two $x_1$ face fluxes of cell $i$ after the positivity
limiter and sedimentation, the face and centroid potentials, and, with $\mathcal K$, $m_1$ in cells $i-1$, $i$ and
$i+1$. The fluxes are the total mass flux, the dry row plus every mass-carrying species row. Physical $x_1$ faces
are the only ones where $\mathcal K$ is zeroed; seams between blocks keep it, reading the exchanged ghost. The
work is explicit and added once per stage. With an implicit scheme and `gravity-work: face` the correction is
added before the solve and the solve carries the face work in its energy row (@sec-ch06-vic); with `face-wallc`
it is swapped in after the solve. @fig-ch06-face-order shows the measured orders.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch06-face-stencil
#| fig-cap: "What the face form reads. (a) Cell i: the potential flux phi F at its two x1 faces (orange triangles) and the centroid potential phi_i (sky-blue dot), weighted by the distances from the centroid to each face. (b) The curvature flux K (bluish-green triangles) at the bottom wall: it is zero on the wall face (vermillion label), so wall cell 0 sees K on one face only; the ghost cell (hatched) is not read."
#| fig-alt: "Two panels: three cells with face markers and a centroid marker; and a wall with a hatched ghost cell, three interior cells and K markers on the two interior faces."
#| echo: false

make_fig()
```

### Code

**A minimal input.** `face` is the default, so the gravity block alone selects it:

```yaml
forcing:
  const-gravity:
    grav1: -9.8          # m s^-2; gravity-work: face is the default
```

The corrected-PE work of @sec-ch06-dwork is then on by default as well; to run the plain face form of this
section, start the run with `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0` in the environment. From `build/bin` of a build at
the pin ([Install and run](#sec-preface-install)), on a deck with this block, such as `straka_single.yaml`:

```bash
SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0 ./straka.release straka_single.yaml
```

**What the parser refuses, and why.** The same three checks as @sec-ch06-cell. Also,
`gravity-work-fixer: true` is refused with `face` when $g_1\ne0$: the fixer repairs the cell form's defect, and the
face form has none ({{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).

One more refusal is raised by the stage itself rather than by the parser, the first time the $\mathcal K$ branch
would run. With a `cp3`, `cp5` or `weno5` $x_1$ reconstruction, the corrected-PE work off, and a grid that
declares a stretched $x_1$, the step throws "the dx^2/12 x1 curvature flux H of cp3/cp5/weno5 is a uniform-grid
device: a stretched x1 uses option F, gravity-work: face with SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT on (the default),
fourth order there; or use gravity-work: cell"
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). The message names the two ways out: leave
`SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT` at its default, so that the corrected-PE work of @sec-ch06-dwork takes over, or
set `gravity-work: cell`. `face-wallc` is not a third: it reaches the same branch and is refused with it, which
is the combination the test below uses. The "fourth order there" of the message is the code's claim for
the corrected-PE work on a stretched grid; what this report has measured on a stretched grid is the fourth-order
convergence of the corrected potential energy $P$ itself, not of the booked work (@sec-ch06-dwork, Limits).
A deck that is merely curved, with equal radial widths, does not trip the refusal: `stretched_x1` is a property
of the grid key ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::stretched_x1 >}}), not of the cell
volumes, so $\mathcal K$ still runs there with the two-point form.

**The code, mapped to @eq-ch06-dwork-face** ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
auto phi_face = -grav1 * pmb->pcoord->x1f;
auto phi_cell = -grav1 * pmb->pcoord->x1v;
auto potential_flux1 = vertical_mass_flux1 * phi_face.narrow(0, 0, vertical_mass_flux1.size(-1));
...
auto face_gravity_work = dt * (phi_cell.slice(0, is, ie) * vertical_mass_div - potential_flux_div);
```

`vertical_mass_div` is $\Delta_i[AF]/V_i$ and `potential_flux_div` is $\Delta_i[A\phi F]/V_i$, formed in the lines elided.
`face_gravity_work` is $\Delta t\,W^{\mathrm{face}}_i$ in the form of step 1; `gravity_energy_correction` then adds it
and removes $W^{\mathrm{cell}}$, @eq-ch06-face-energy.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| mass and potential fluxes | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `potential_flux1` | `gravity-work` |
| face work | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `face_gravity_work` | `gravity-work` |
| curvature flux | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `curv_flux1` | `reconstruct`[^rg-22ada5ab295b] |
| face minus cell, wall cells | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `gravity_energy_correction` | `face-wallc` |
| x1 wall test | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::is_x1_wall >}} | `is_x1_wall` | |
| implicit warning | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}} | `face_work_in_operator` | `implicit-scheme` |

: Code map of the face form. {#tbl-ch06-face-code}

1. Sum the total $x_1$ mass flux over the dry and species rows as `vertical_mass_flux1`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
2. Form the face and cell potentials and the two divergences in `potential_flux_div`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
3. Book the face work as `face_gravity_work` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
4. Subtract the curvature flux for cp3, cp5 and weno5, zeroed at physical faces, as `curv_flux1`, after refusing
   the combination on a declared stretched $x_1$
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
5. Replace the cell work, keeping it in the wall cells under `face-wallc`, as `gravity_energy_correction`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

A user can hit the setup warning "gravity-work: face-wallc with an implicit scheme: the face work sits outside the
implicit operator" (also for `face` with `implicit-scheme: 0`).

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_forcing.release` | curvature excess removed | $10^{-9}$ abs. | test threshold |
| `test_forcing.release` | no horizontal mass divergence | $10^{-10}$ rel. | test threshold |
| `test_gravity_work_fixer_python` | face-wallc arm, reported | n/a | reported only |
| `test_implicit_face_work_operator_python` | rest column, Courant 66-657 | $10^{-11}$ | `EPE_TOL` |
| `test_stretched_x1_ref.release`, `refuses_curvature_correction` and `refuses_curvature_correction_cp5` | a stretched `weno5` or `cp5` column with `gravity-work: face-wallc` throws with the message above, and the uniform twin of the same deck runs | exact (throws or not) | a setup contract |
| `test_stretched_x1_ref_radial_exact_off.release` (`SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0`) | the same refusal with the plain face form and the default `gravity-work` | exact (throws) | a setup contract |
| same file, `uniform_and_stretched_reflecting_decks_run` | with the switch at its default, the stretched `weno5` column runs | exact (does not throw) | the way out named in the message |

: Tests of the face form; assertions read from the test sources at the pin, not run. {#tbl-ch06-face-tests}

`[C1]` of `cellface_check.py` measures the conservation of the four steps; `[C3]` and `[C4]` the orders, 2.00 in all
cells without $\mathcal K$ and 3.99 interior, 1.00 wall with it; `[C5]` the `face-wallc` defect.

`vertical_gravity_work_removes_the_curvature_excess` sets a quadratic $m_1$ on six cells. It requires the off-wall
excess to equal $\Delta t\,\tfrac{h^2}{12}\cdot2\cdot0.04\cdot0.03$ for cp3 and five-point reconstructions
and zero otherwise, to $10^{-9}$ absolute, as `expected` ({{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp vertical_gravity_work_removes_the_curvature_excess >}}). The
plain face form is tested with `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0` set in the registration
(`set_tests_properties` in {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}). The curvature test also has a CUDA[^rg-dd629466f3e7] case.
Measured values at the pin are **missing evidence**.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
With an implicit scheme, the face work must be inside the implicit operator; `face-wallc` books it after the solve,
and a tall column then blows up. The onset depends on the acoustic Courant number and on $N\Delta t$,
with $N$ the buoyancy (Brunt–Väisälä) frequency [s$^{-1}$], so that $N\Delta t$ is the time step in units of the buoyancy period over $2\pi$ (@tbl-ch06-vic-onset); acoustic Courant about 66 holds only for the 45-cell column it was found on.[^ch06-face-283]
:::

[^ch06-face-283]: The tall-column blow-up is recorded in chengcli/snapy#283.

- The work is $O(h^2)$ in every cell without $\mathcal K$, and first order in the wall cells with it.
- $\mathcal K$ is a uniform-grid device. On a declared stretched $x_1$ it is refused; on a curved grid with equal
  radial widths, where the cell measure is $r^2\,\mathrm{d}r$ and the cell volumes are unequal
  (@sec-ch04-x1volume), it is not refused and its two-point form is not exact. That case is not measured.
- `face-wallc` does not conserve $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ in its two wall cells (`[C5]`).
- The orders above use exact point fluxes; with the scheme's own fluxes the reconstruction and Riemann errors add.
- Combinations with the study switches: @sec-ch12-matrix.

[^rg-bf06c25d4aa7]: $n_1, n_2, n_3$ — interior cells per block in each direction

[^rg-22ada5ab295b]: reconstruct — reconstruction options
